_note: Hooks written by Claude from references/hooks.md (types 8, 4, 11, 3). Each is true to the research file.

options.spoken: يقولون إن رولكس صنعت أول ساعة يدٍ مقاومةٍ للماء… والحقيقة أذكى من ذلك.
options.visual: Frame 1: the question in big type drops onto paper; a red stamp «ليس تمامًا» slams down at 1.2 s.
options.pays_off: l2 (earlier watches) and l13 (Rolex did not invent it; it made the world trust it)

options.spoken: أكتوبر، عام سبعةٍ وعشرين. سبّاحةٌ في بحرٍ بارد… وعلى معصمها ساعة رولكس.
options.visual: Frame 1: layered paper waves already moving under a cold moon, camera pushing in.

options.spoken: انظر إلى التاج في جانب الساعة… هذا الجزء الصغير غيّر قصة رولكس.
options.visual: Frame 1: a pencil section of a crown on its tube, the crown already moving in.
options.pays_off: l3-l7 (the crown problem and the screw-down crown)

options.spoken: أكثر من عشر ساعات في ماء البحر… وساعة رولكس لم تتوقف.
options.visual: Frame 1: a stopwatch sweeping over paper waves.

reasons: It names the icon (Rolex) in the first second, it corrects a belief many viewers hold, and it is true: the research says earlier water-resistant wristwatches existed (claim c4) and the hook only reports the belief («يقولون»). The film pays it off twice (l2, l13). For a watch dealer, correcting a myth builds trust. H2 is more cinematic but does not say what the film is about until l5; H4 risks implying the watch was underwater for ten hours by design.
